question: Can a held-scene-excluded deterministic density-domain difference-of-Gaussians acutance operator explain useful B&W film residual structure better than basic, linear-luma, and wrong-radius controls?

analysis.selection: leave-one-scene-out minimum median normalized radial-PSD error; lexicographic tie break
analysis.linear_control: same selected sigmas and strength applied as a mean-zero linear-luma DoG
analysis.wrong_radius_control: same selected strength with both sigmas doubled

branches.pass: retain one generic deterministic density-domain acutance candidate and open full-resolution severe-artifact visual comparison
branches.fail: close fitted spatial-response use of this source and retain BP2 as descriptive display-chain evidence only
branches.control_fail: classify any gain as generic digital sharpening rather than density-domain evidence

forbidden: retune grids thresholds or controls after formal execution
use held-film pixels to choose its operator parameters
claim stock emulsion developer process scanner calibration or product evidence
use hard clipping or an unconstrained sharpening operator
open visual review when any automatic gate fails
claim_ceiling: leave-one-scene-out generic B&W display-chain acutance mechanism feasibility; target-informed tone baseline and one-author data prevent product, stock, emulsion, developer, process, scanner or calibration claims
